lesson.title: Read the bars
lesson.subtitle: P3 bridge and P4 bar-chart revision
lesson.objective: Work out the scale of a bar chart, read a bar and add two bars.
lesson.story: The bar chart shows pets chosen by pupils: Cats, Dogs, Fish, Birds and Mice. The scale goes up in equal steps.

steps.title: Work out the scale
steps.prompt: Only the bottom and top gridlines have numbers. What does each gap between two gridlines stand for?
hints: Look at the numbers written beside the axis, then at the lines between them.
Count the equal gaps between the bottom line and the top line.
The top line is 120 and there are 6 equal gaps. Share 120 equally between the gaps.

steps.title: Read one bar
steps.prompt: How tall is the Cats bar? Read its value from the scale.
hints: Find the Cats bar and look at where its top edge ends.
Follow the top of the bar across to the axis. The gridlines help your eye.
The top of the Cats bar is halfway between the gridlines for 40 and 60.

steps.title: Add two bars
steps.prompt: What is the total of the Cats bar and the Mice bar?
hints: Read each bar on its own first.
Read the Cats bar and the Mice bar with the scale of 20.
Cats is 50 and Mice is 110. Add the two numbers.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why do you work out the scale before you read a bar?

choices.label: Not every line has a number, so the gap size tells you each value.
The scale always goes up in ones, so you can just count the lines up.
The tallest bar sets the scale, so you read every other bar from it.

hints: Think about the numbers you could see beside the axis.
Only the bottom and top lines had numbers.
The size of a gap lets you name every line between them.
Choose the explanation about the size of each gap.
